claims.text: The baseline refractory high-entropy alloy contains Nb, Mo, Ta, and W.
Vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization yields a single-phase BCC baseline alloy.
Adding approximately 0.5–1.0 wt% yttrium will form in situ Y2O3 nanoprecipitates during high-temperature annealing.
The yttrium addition and resulting nanoprecipitates will not alter the primary BCC alloy phase.
The intervention will produce a dispersion of thermally stable Y2O3 nanoparticles within the BCC matrix.
Y2O3 nano-oxide dispersoids impede dislocation motion.
Y2O3 nano-oxide dispersoids suppress radiation-enhanced defect migration.
Impeded dislocation motion and suppressed defect migration enhance strength and creep resistance.
The high formation energy of the dispersoids limits their coarsening during prolonged high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
Limited dispersoid coarsening preserves the alloy's thermal and irradiation stability.
Relative to the yttrium-free baseline, the yttrium-modified alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength.
Relative to the yttrium-free baseline, the yttrium-modified alloy will have a lower elevated-temperature creep rate.
The yttrium-modified alloy will maintain phase and microstructural stability under irradiation.
The proposed improvements will hold at service temperatures up to approximately 1000°C.
The proposed improvements will hold under radiation doses typical of high-temperature reactor or space environments.
Excessive yttrium content could cause grain-boundary embrittlement.
Exposure beyond the proposed limits could cause dispersoid coarsening and nullify the mechanical benefits.
